what: A character or icon walks straight (linear) for dist px at speed px/s, then returns at the same speed, repeating endlessly. It flips scaleX at every turn so it always faces the direction of travel. Use it to let walking Lottie or SVG people loose over a town illustration (give each person a different distance and speed so the streets feel busy).

options.dir: right (default) or left — direction it walks first
options.flip: If false, left and right are not flipped when turning around

parts.body: (if present) inner element to move — if absent the element itself moves. Used to leave the outer one free for other transforms such as scroll parallax

use: (Walking Lottie·SVG)

from.where: index.js peopleAc·peopleAcReturn — 32 people go back and forth following a [distance, speed, direction] table (e.g. 1500px·30px/s·right, rickshaw 2000px·60px/s·left), Lottie walks start at random frames at 1.2~1.7x speed

index.css .t-bus (the school bus under the bus route text box — travels 40rem (400px at 1440) and back over 28s, flipping at the halfway point = dist: 400; speed: 28.6 · the original layers one more .8s rattle on top (gatagata: −2px at 20%, −1px at 55%, cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1.3)) — this part lacks it, so it is layered in the site css)

note: The original runs the walking figure with lottie-web (loop), and only the back-and-forth this part does was done in GSAP. The walking artwork is supplied by the consumer and placed inside body
